newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up, waiver on U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up, waiver on U.S. long bond.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended slightly higher on Wednesday, rebounding from a four-day loss after a rough ride on the back of a fluctuating U.S. bond market.
"The market is volatile in line with Wall Street, despite mild retail sales and producer prices data," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
"Fears of U.S. inflation persist, and the market will be cautious until the (Aug. 19) Fed meeting," he added.
The leading IPC share index was up 13.75 points, or 0.28 percent, at 5,016.63.

The IPC had reached as high as 5,087.31 points in early trade then dipped to a low of 4,969.11 points on profit-taking triggered by a slide on Wall Street. The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 32.52 points at 7,928.32.

The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond, meanwhile, trimmed an early rise of 1-1/4 point to end 17/32 higher, reducing its yield to 6.63 percent from Tuesday's close of 6.67 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
On the broad market, gainers outnumbered decliners by 50 to 45, out of a total of 119 stocks that changed hands. Volume of 100.1 million shares traded was slower than many recent sessions.
"We moved on thin volume, the market is cautious and waiting for more keynote U.S. data," a floor trader said, referring to retail price data due early Thursday.

Dealers said falling 30-year bond yields outweighed the effect on financial stocks of Tuesday night's increase in Cetes, or domestic treasury bond, rates. "Cetes rate hikes are expected to be temporary," a desk trader said.

Mexico's two biggest financial groups, Bancomer and Banamex-Accival, both ended up. Bancomer gained 54 centavos (7 cents to 5.60 pesos (72 cents), while Banamex-Accival rose 1.15 pesos (15 cents) to 23.90 pesos ($3.07).
Cement company Cemex gained 40 centavos (5 cents) to 41.70 pesos ($5.36) as investors counted the lower cost of paying its dollar debt after the fall in the U.S. long bond yield, traders said.

Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) weighed heaviest on the market, dealers said, falling 5 centavos (less than 1 cent) to 20.20 pesos ($2.60) in brisk trade. Telmex American Depostary Receipts, meanwhile, shed 5/16 to end at 51-11/16.
Holding company Synkro headed the percentage gainers list, rising 9 centavos (1 cent) to 25 (3 cents) as Synkro commercial paper may be exchanged for stock in the company on Aug. 21, analysts noted.
